slides.title: What does it take for you to say sorry and mean it?

body.text: This is your question for today. Keep it in mind during the games.
Three games tonight: standing, guarded, pinned. Win one and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run the same one again.
Hand Fight with Dual Win Conditions
Skill Learning Objective (SLO): Entering, for both players.
Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both hand fighting at the wrists, elbows, and head.
Win one of two ways: collect three touches in any mix, or get an underhook and close your hands around your partner's shoulders, body, or leg.

items: Whoever gets there first wins, whether by three touches or by the underhook plus closed hands.

body.text: Guard Recovery with Passing Resistance Game
SLO: Arriving for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The bottom player is lying on his side. The top player has passed the legs and is at his hips.

Bottom player: stay mobile on your side, stop the top player's hands from connecting, and get your legs back in front. Top player: lock your hands around the bottom player's waist, chest, or back to stop the recovery.

items: The bottom player wins by recovering to any real guard position while staying mobile.
The top player wins by locking his hands.

body.text: Figure Four, Reintroduction with Hand-to-Mat or Knuckles-Behind Win
SLO: Finishing for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The bottom player is in side control, chest to chest. The top player starts with a figure-four grip on one arm, under his elbow.

Top player: stay under the elbow, even if you lose the hand for a moment, and put the bottom player's palm flat on the mat or his knuckles behind his back. Bottom player: fight the grip directly and get the figure four out from under your elbow.

items: The top player wins by palm to mat or knuckles behind the back.
The bottom player wins by removing the figure four from under the elbow.

slides.title: How you win it
slides.question: In Figure Four, Reintroduction with Hand-to-Mat or Knuckles-Behind Win, what wins it for the top player?

options.text: The top player wins by palm to mat or knuckles behind the back.
options.feedback: That is the win condition, and nothing else scores.

options.text: Holding the finish after your partner taps
options.feedback: Never. Let go the instant your partner taps. Every single time. The tap is law.
You keep the pin by feeling your partner and moving with them, not by clamping down and squeezing hard. Staying calm beats forcing harder.

slides.correctText: That is how you win today.
